verification_method: ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 posted results (live fetch, 2026-07-30) + PubMed abstracts of the primary publications. Every count below was read off one of those two surfaces; nothing is back-computed from a percentage and nothing is imputed.

headline_defect.claim_removed: Pooled RR 2.44 (0.47-12.82) and every quantity derived from it (heterogeneity, Bayesian posterior, TSA, NNT/NNH, GRADE, fragility index, funnel/Egger, L'Abbe, plain-language 'increased risk by about 144%', manuscript conclusion).
headline_defect.why_invalid: The pooled estimate combined (a) ISTH major bleeding after gynaecologic-cancer surgery, apixaban 1/204 vs enoxaparin 1/196, with (b) RAMBLE's 3/8 vs 1/11, which is neither the PBAC primary outcome nor an apixaban-vs-control contrast - it is the SECONDARY outcome 'crossed over to another anticoagulant', with the 3/8 arm being RIVAROXABAN. The two quantities measure different phenomena and the second is direction-reversed. No valid two-trial meta-analysis exists over this set.
headline_defect.value_was_not_hardcoded: RR 2.44 and RAMBLE's RR 4.13 are computed at runtime from the ledger; the only occurrence of the literal string '2.44' in the file is a coefficient inside the normalQuantile rational approximation. The fix is therefore at the data + gate layer, not a string replacement.

trials.label: RAMBLE
trials.question: E. Menstrual blood loss in menstruating patients anticoagulated for VTE or AF (apixaban vs rivaroxaban)
trials.status: RETAINED as a standalone, severely underpowered continuous-outcome pilot. Three extraction errors corrected.
sources: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02829957 posted results, API v2, fetched 2026-07-30 (registry is the only source; no journal publication of RAMBLE was found on PubMed)
Registry document section: Study Protocol (Prot_000.pdf) AND Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP_001.pdf) are both attached
trials.design: Randomised open-label, Indiana University, 19 participants. Rivaroxaban 15 mg BID x7d then 20 mg daily vs apixaban 10 mg BID x7d then 5 mg BID, 3 months. Registered PHASE2/PHASE3. Start 2016-09, primary completion 2020-02-13.
trials.registry_flow_group_order: FG000 = Rivaroxaban (STARTED 8), FG001 = Apixaban (STARTED 11). The intervention is listed SECOND. This is the mechanism of the arm reversal.

a_outcome_type.was: PBAC treated as a binary event outcome, 3/8 vs 1/11, RR 4.13
a_outcome_type.is: PBAC Scores is the PRIMARY outcome and is a CONTINUOUS/ordinal score. Registry paramType = MEDIAN, dispersion = Full Range, unit = 'score on a scale'. Rivaroxaban median 292 (range 74-600), n=6; apixaban median 146 (range 3-378), n=10.
a_outcome_type.handling: Recorded as a CONTINUOUS outcome with tE/cE null so the app renders its continuous-outcome panel. No mean difference or SMD is computed: medians with full ranges at n=6 and n=10 cannot be converted to mean/SD without fabricating a distributional assumption on a heavily skewed score.

b_wrong_outcome.was: the counts 3 and 1 were labelled 'PBAC Scores (primary)'
b_wrong_outcome.is: 3 and 1 are the SECONDARY outcome 'Number of Participants Who Crossed Over to Another Anticoagulant' (rivaroxaban 3/8, apixaban 1/11). PBAC contributes no count rows at all, being a median outcome.
b_wrong_outcome.root_cause: outputs/new_topics/APIXABAN_VTE_AUTO.json stores aact_outcome_count_rows as a FLAT, unlabelled list of (group, value) pairs across all outcomes, and the builder bound the first pair to aact_primary_outcome_measure. For RAMBLE the first pair is the crossover outcome.

c_arm_reversal.is: 3/8 is the RIVAROXABAN arm; 1/11 is apixaban
c_arm_reversal.root_cause: The same corpus file stores aact_per_arm_counts as {BG000: 8, BG001: 11} and the builder assumes baseline group index 0 is the intervention. For RAMBLE, group 0 is rivaroxaban.
c_arm_reversal.consequence: The displayed RR 4.13 was neither a PBAC effect nor an apixaban-vs-control estimate. Corrected direction for the crossover outcome: apixaban 1/11 vs rivaroxaban 3/8, RR 0.242.

year_correction.why: The corpus matched RAMBLE to PMID 26272306 (De Crem N et al., Thromb Res 2015;136:749-53, 'Abnormal uterine bleeding in VTE patients treated with rivaroxaban compared to vitamin K antagonists'). That is a single-centre RETROSPECTIVE questionnaire study of rivaroxaban vs vitamin K antagonists - not RAMBLE, not randomised, not apixaban. It appears in RAMBLE's registry record as a BACKGROUND citation, and the matcher took a background reference as the trial's own publication. RAMBLE started 2016-09 and completed 2020-02-13; year set to 2020 (primary completion) with the registry as the source and no publication claimed.

review_claims_adjudicated.evidence: The continuous-outcome panel is gated on tE and cE both being null, which was not true for either trial as previously recorded. What the app actually did was the OPPOSITE error - it rendered RAMBLE's genuinely continuous PBAC primary as a binary event count. The caption defect the review describes is the visible symptom of that inversion.

defects_found_this_session_not_in_the_re.finding: RAMBLE is matched to the wrong publication. PMID 26272306 is De Crem 2015, a retrospective rivaroxaban-vs-VKA questionnaire study taken from RAMBLE's own BACKGROUND citation list. This is the source of the app's RAMBLE year of 2015.
Because that wrong publication is dated 2015, the pre-2015 protocol filter admitted RAMBLE on a false date. The filter that excluded AMPLIFY admitted RAMBLE only by an extraction error.

Both trials had their registry phase overwritten to 'III'. NCT02366871 is registered PHASE2 and RAMBLE is PHASE2/PHASE3. The app separately auto-excludes phase-II-like records from analysis, so the mislabel is what kept the gynaecologic trial in the analysis at all.
NCT02366871 has TWO co-primary outcomes (major bleeding and CRNM bleeding). Only one was recorded, so the co-primary showing 12/204 vs 19/196 was invisible.

The corpus matched NCT02366871 to PMID 32641236, which is the medication-adherence subanalysis (Ross 2020, Gynecol Oncol), not the primary RCT report. The app's own ledger happened to carry the correct PMID 32589230, so the two disagree.

The in-page CT.gov auto-extraction engine identifies the intervention arm with the regex /apixaban_vte_auto|bay\s*94|treatment|active/i. 'bay 94' is the finerenone development code. On any apixaban trial this regex cannot match the drug name and falls through to positional/keyword guesses. This is a live extraction hazard, not only a cosmetic one.
The Arabic localisation table contains cardiorenal template strings, including a mapping of the topic slug to the Arabic word for finerenone and 'Primary Result' rendered as 'Primary MACE result'.
